exposure: mode of birth (vaginal delivery, cesarean section)
cohort: The study included 227 women with urinary incontinence who were receiving treatment at a reference outpatient unit in the South of Brazil.
finding: Mixed urinary incontinence was the predominant subtype, and multiparity and vaginal delivery characterized this group of women with urinary incontinence, although no statistical significance was found between the incontinence subtypes and the gestational history variables.
mod_finding: Vaginal deliveries (two or more) were more frequent (71.4%) than cesarean sections (14.5%) for women with two or more pregnancies in the studied group with urinary incontinence, but no statistical significance was found between incontinence subtypes and mode of birth.
cross-section timing: During treatment at a reference outpatient unit for urinary incontinence.
